newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Emergency U.N. Mideast session delayed to next week.
newsitem.headline: Emergency U.N. Mideast session delayed to next week.

text.p: An emergency special session of the General Assembly on Israeli building in East Jerusalem, which had been expected to get under way on Monday, will probably be delayed a week, diplomats said.
This is because the request for the session by the Arab group of states has not yet been formally endorsed by the required majority of the assembly's 185 members.

A U.N. spokesman said on Monday a total of 60 letters of support, of the 93 needed to trigger an emergency session within 24 hours, had so far been received by the U.N. secretariat. The session is expected to last two days.

One reason for postponing it until next Monday, even if the required number of requests is received by mid-week, is because the Moslem feast of Eid al-Adha, which is a U.N. staff holiday, will be observed on Thursday.

The session was requested at the end of March under a 1950 "uniting for peace" procedure that enables an issue considered to be a threat to international peace to be transferred to the assembly if action by the Security Council has been blocked by a veto.

Vetoes by the United States, on March 7 and March 21, prevented the adoption of a council resolution calling on Israel to abandon plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a site between Jerusalem and Bethlehem called Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic and Har Homa in Hebrew. Israel captured the area in the 1967 Middle East War.

The request for the session was supported by the 113-member non-aligned movement at a recent meeting in New Delhi, as well as by the Organisation of the Islamic Conference. But states must individually notify the U.N. secretariat of their backing.
